items.question: What is CIEL AVENUE?
items.answer: CIEL AVENUE is a tool under construction that helps structure a property project: gathering a property's information, comparing options and preparing discussions with professionals. It is not yet open to the public.

items.question: Who is the pilot for?
items.answer: Individuals who own a property or plan to buy, and the real estate professionals who support them, in Rennes and Ille-et-Vilaine. Participation terms will be specified before launch.

items.question: What is the Property Passport?
items.answer: A structured file gathering a home's information: available or missing documents, surveys, works, options considered. It is being designed and will be built with pilot participants.

items.question: When will the service be available?
items.answer: No date has been set yet. A prototype with fictitious data can be viewed; the pilot is in preparation.

items.question: How do I get pilot updates?
items.answer: The "Get pilot updates" button opens your email app with a prefilled message to the team. No data is collected on this site: you choose what you write to us.

items.question: Can Céleste advise me?
items.answer: No. Céleste is a planned assistant to help organise information and prepare questions. It does not replace legal, technical or financial advice from qualified professionals.

story.title: How it started: a need observed in the field.
paragraphs: Experience on building sites and in structuring Guillotin Peinture Père & Fils, then involvement in Guillotin Immo, brought Timon into contact with decisions that span several trades.
The observation behind the project: documents that exist but are scattered; decisions made at different times; and context lost between the owner, the building site and property management.
CIEL AVENUE aims to connect these steps. The Property Passport and option preparation are the intended tools to make this common thread concrete.

founder.headline: Carrying the vision and deciding what should be built.
bio: Timon sets the project's direction, structures the strategy and leads the trade-offs. The challenge: keep field needs, product scope and rollout conditions consistent.
His experience drives one principle: a platform only has value if it helps owners and professionals prepare a real decision or intervention.

items.answer: The loss of continuity between documents, decisions and interventions. The founder's field experience, between building sites and property management, shapes this problem.

start.description: Buying, renovating, renting or selling: your documents and questions are often scattered. Start by organising what you already know.

before.label: Before
before.text: Emails, attachments and conversations with no overview.

after.label: After
after.text: A goal, an indicative budget, the useful documents and a list of questions to handle.

documents.title: Find and check your documents
documents.description: Start with what you already have. Examples of often useful documents:
items: Title deed or preliminary sale agreement
Surveys (EPC, electrical, gas, asbestos…)
Floor plans
Invoices and warranties for past works
Property tax and service charges
Co-ownership: rules and latest general meeting minutes
Quotes already received
documents.warning: Having a document doesn't mean it's up to date: check its date and source. The relevant professional will tell you what needs updating.

options.title: Compare what each option involves
options.description: For each path, note what remains to check: feasibility, intended cost, constraints and timing.

items.name: Buy
questions: What overall budget: price, notary fees, works?
What should be checked before making an offer?

items.name: Renovate
questions: Which works, in what order, and is a permit needed?
What budget and timeline to consider?

items.name: Rent out
questions: Does the home meet letting requirements, especially energy ones?
Furnished or unfurnished: what difference does it make for you?

items.name: Sell
questions: Which documents should the sale file include?
What timeframe and price to consider, and who to ask?

options.warning: These questions help prepare your conversations. They don't replace a valuation, a quote or professional advice.

next.title: Choose one thing to do now
next.description: Once your documents and options are laid out, the next step becomes concrete:
items: Request the missing document
Prepare 3 to 5 questions for a professional
Book a first meeting (tradesperson, agency, notary, bank or broker as needed)
next.example: Example: "Ask the seller for the EPC before Saturday's visit, and list my questions about the heating."

steps.title: Your project is prepared at every step.
steps.description: You move forward from the information available, identifying the checks to make before each decision. The journey never pushes you faster than your situation allows.

items.title: Your situation
items.description: Your goal, your timeframe and the constraints you already know.
todo: Write your goal in one sentence
Estimate a budget, even roughly
Set a timeframe: under 3 months, this year, later

items.title: Property Passport
items.description: Documents available, missing or to check.
todo: List the documents you already have
Note those missing and who to ask
Check dates: an old survey may need redoing

items.title: Options to explore
items.description: Buy, renovate, rent out or sell: the questions specific to each.
todo: Keep two or three realistic paths
For each, note intended cost, time and constraints
Drop what doesn't fit your budget or timeframe

items.title: Decision to prepare
todo: List what must be true for the option to work
Identify who can confirm each assumption
Sign nothing before these checks

items.title: Project framework
todo: Describe what's included and what isn't
Draw up a simple timeline
Allow a margin for the unexpected

items.title: Professionals
items.description: Expertise to involve and questions to ask.
todo: Pick the right person for the question: technical, legal or financial
Send a clear summary before the meeting
Compare several quotes where possible

items.title: Follow-up and review
todo: Tick off what's done
Keep new documents (invoices, certificates, surveys)
Note what's still open

questions.question: Which documents should I find?
questions.answer: Start with what you already have. The relevant professional will say what's missing for your decision.

questions.question: What should I check before choosing?
questions.answer: Constraints, feasibility and intended costs should be examined before picking an option.

questions.question: Who should I ask next?
questions.answer: Depending on the topic: a tradesperson or architect for works, an agency for renting or selling, a notary for legal matters, a bank or broker for financing.

faq.title: Your questions before a purchase, works or a decision about your property.

items.question: I don't know yet whether to renovate, rent or sell. Can I start?
items.answer: Yes. Start with your goal, an indicative budget and your constraints. The options can then be examined with the relevant professionals.

items.question: I'm preparing a first purchase: where do I start?
items.answer: Clarify your overall budget (price, notary fees, any works), your must-haves and your timeframe. Before an offer, ask for the surveys and, in a co-ownership, the latest general meeting minutes. Your bank or a broker can specify your borrowing capacity.

items.question: Which documents should I find for my property?
items.answer: The ones you already have: title deed, plans, surveys, works invoices, property tax, co-ownership documents. Having them doesn't mean they're up to date: a professional will say what needs updating.

items.question: How do I estimate my budget and timeline?
items.answer: Start from a range, even a wide one, and a timeframe (under 3 months, this year, later). Allow a margin for the unexpected. Precise amounts will come from professionals' quotes, valuations and simulations.

items.question: Does the Property Passport replace a survey?
items.answer: No. It's intended as a file to organise information, not a technical, energy or regulatory survey.

items.question: Can Céleste tell me which works to do?
items.answer: No. The planned assistant helps prepare information and questions. It doesn't replace a technical visit, a feasibility study, a quote or professional advice.

items.question: Who will be able to see my file?
items.answer: Access rules, uses and retention periods will be defined before any real data collection. No file is shared today.

items.question: Can I create an account already?
items.answer: No. The pilot is in preparation and no personal space is open. A prototype with fictitious data only lets you visualise the journey.

items.question: Is the Discovery offer available yet?
items.answer: Not yet. The €0 price is provisional; the offer's content, terms and opening date are still to be confirmed.

context.title: Context, not just a pile of documents.
context.description: The Property Passport aims to link documents to the project, keeping their source, date and points to check:
items: Client goal and intended use of the property
Documents available, missing or to update
Expected checks and who owns them
Responsibilities and next action
context.boundary: Access limited to the documents the client authorises for your assignment: no universal access, no automatic validation of documents.

celeste.questionsTitle: Three questions to prepare what comes next

questions.question: Which documents does my work require?
questions.answer: Your trade determines the useful documents and checks. The file helps request them, within the access the client grants.

questions.question: What is blocking the scoping?
questions.answer: A goal, a document or an approval may be missing. The point is to make it explicit and identify who should handle it.

questions.question: Who owns the next action?
questions.answer: Specify the expected action, the person responsible and the conditions for moving forward.

celeste.note: The client keeps the decision, you keep responsibility for your opinions. Céleste doesn't replace any qualified professional.

benefits.title: What the file should make more usable for your trade.
benefits.description: Examples of uses the pilot should test, not proven results.

brief.title: A better-framed request
brief.description: Client goal, intended use and limits of your assignment: an explicit starting point.
brief.example: Example: before travelling, a surveyor knows whether the property is in a co-ownership, its approximate size and which surveys already exist.

documents.title: Documents to examine, not guess
documents.description: Identify available documents and request missing ones, within authorisations.
documents.example: Example: a tradesperson sees the plans exist but the EPC is over ten years old, and flags it before quoting.

followUp.title: Clearer follow-up
followUp.description: Clarify expected actions, approvals to obtain and what to pass on to the next party.
followUp.example: Example: an estate agent knows the listing is waiting for the works completion certificate, and who must provide it.

items.question: Who can apply for the pilot?
items.answer: The pilot targets property and construction professionals working in Rennes and Ille-et-Vilaine: surveyors, tradespeople, estate agents, architects, notaries, property managers… Admission criteria are still to be defined: applying doesn't mean admission.

items.question: What works today?
items.answer: A prototype with fictitious data can be viewed. The Property Passport and file sharing are being designed; the Céleste assistant is planned. No professional space is open.

items.question: Which documents will I be able to access?
items.answer: Only those the client authorises for your assignment, under rules to be defined before any real sharing. No full access to the client file is planned by default.

items.question: Does the file replace my own checks?
items.answer: No. You keep the checks, obligations and responsibilities of your trade. A document in the file doesn't validate its content.

items.question: How are responsibilities split?
items.answer: Each assignment's scope, deliverables and approvals are agreed between you and the client. The file makes these explicit; it doesn't transfer responsibility.

items.question: Does the platform guarantee me assignments?
items.answer: No. No volume of projects, revenue, meetings or conversion rate is guaranteed. CIEL AVENUE is not presented as a lead provider.

items.question: How do I apply and how does onboarding work?
items.answer: Describe your company, trade, area and the coordination need to test. The current form is a demonstration that sends nothing; pilot onboarding will be specified when it opens.

items.question: What are the commercial terms?
items.answer: The Expert Pro and Organisation Pilot offers are shown with provisional prices. Content, pricing and terms are still to be confirmed.

items.question: What would Céleste do in a professional journey?
items.answer: The planned assistant would help structure the brief, spot missing documents and prepare follow-ups. It produces no professional approval or commitment on your behalf, and its suggestions need checking.
